acceptanceCriteria.text: Fireguard grading runs across at least two parallel CI jobs/shards using the same HEAD/base; workload partitioning preserves the complete grading workload and existing gate semantics without duplicate full grading runs.
The normal test CI workload runs across parallel jobs/shards and collectively executes every app/scripts and Fireguard unit-test file, without unintentionally omitting or duplicating test files.
The test CI path no longer invokes coverage collection or enforces coverage thresholds; the opt-in local coverage command remains available.

Required status checks named test and fireguard reflect all shards: any failed/missing shard or tool error fails the relevant check; existing triggers, skip-ci behavior and deployment gating remain intact.

Fireguard emits one combined report/grade and one sticky PR comment, correctly combining shard counts; representative sharded and unsharded runs agree on grading totals and verdict, and failure-path verification is recorded.

CI/Fireguard documentation describes shard commands and concurrency; targeted behavioral checks, workflow validation, representative runtime smoke evidence and the applicable standalone delivery gates pass and are recorded.

body:
## Outcome
Reduce CI wall-clock time by distributing Fireguard grading and the test suite across parallel GitHub Actions jobs, without dropping tests or weakening grading. Remove coverage enforcement from the test CI path. This request is to create the card only; execution waits for a separate launch.

## Current behavior
`.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` has one Windows `test` job that runs `npm test` followed by `npm run coverage`, re-running app tests with coverage thresholds. `npm test` runs the app/scripts Vitest suite and then Fireguard's own Vitest suite sequentially. One Ubuntu `fireguard` job grades the committed diff and posts a sticky PR comment. Fireguard already has internal concurrent snapshot lanes; DM-484 addresses those internal speedups. This card is specifically CI-level splitting, not a duplicate lane rewrite or a dependency on DM-484.

## Change
- Split Fireguard's grading workload into deterministic parallel CI shards/jobs using the existing isolated lane machinery. Every shard must use the same committed HEAD and base ref. Reuse existing concurrency controls and bound nested workers to avoid oversubscribing runners. Preserve gate semantics, 100 configured flake runs, changed-line mutation scope, and failure/tool-error handling; do not make mutation interference invalidate flake results.
- Split the normal test CI workload into parallel shards/jobs, covering the app/scripts suite and Fireguard's own suite. Use native Vitest sharding where suitable; choose and document a conservative shard count. Avoid running the full suite redundantly in every shard. Preserve Windows test coverage of supported behavior.
- Remove `npm run coverage` and coverage-threshold enforcement from the test CI path. Keep the opt-in local coverage command/configuration unless a change is strictly necessary for this CI cutover. Do not remove tests or relax test assertions, Fireguard thresholds, lint, typecheck, deadcode or build gates.
- Aggregate results so any failed/missing shard or tool error fails its required check. Preserve the required status-check names `test` and `fireguard` through aggregate jobs if job names change. All grading shards contribute to one correct combined grade/report and one sticky PR comment; shard jobs must not race to overwrite it. Combine mutation counts before scoring rather than averaging shard percentages.
- Preserve current PR/push triggers, skip-ci behavior, base-ref selection and deployment gating. Update CI and Fireguard documentation with shard commands, aggregation and local reproduction.

## Tests
For any new testable sharding/report-aggregation logic, write failing behavioral tests first: disjoint and exhaustive workload partitioning (including uneven/empty partitions), unchanged combined grading totals/verdict compared with unsharded execution, and failure propagation for failed/missing shards. Reuse existing test conventions; do not add tests that merely match YAML/source strings. For workflow-only changes use workflow validation plus execution evidence, not source-text assertions.

## Verification
Exercise the actual sharded commands and aggregate results on a representative committed diff with graded tests and production changes; compare selected tests, configured/executed flake runs, mutation totals and grade with the unsharded equivalent. Demonstrate a failing test/grading shard makes the required aggregate fail, with diagnostic evidence retained. Record commands, shard count and observed elapsed times without claiming unobserved GitHub Actions behavior. Run the full standalone delivery gate: lint, npm test, Fireguard when unit tests are added/modified, typecheck, deadcode and build. Validate the workflow and, when available, attach a real CI run showing overlapping jobs and no coverage step.

## Out of scope
Product behavior, arbitrary grading-threshold changes, removing local coverage tooling, and unrelated Fireguard performance work from DM-484.
expectedArtifacts: Updated .github/workflows/pr-checks.yml with parallel test/Fireguard work and required aggregate checks
Necessary Fireguard sharding/report aggregation implementation and behavioral regression tests
Updated README.md and fireguard/README.md CI and reproduction guidance
Verification evidence: exercised shard commands, combined results, failure propagation and elapsed times
title: Split Fireguard and tests into parallel CI jobs and remove the CI coverage check
